source_title: Strategic Navigation or Stochastic Search? How Agents and Humans Reason Over Document Collections

concepts.label: madqa benchmark
concepts.description: A collection of 2,250 human-written questions based on 800 real PDF documents, designed to test whether AI agents can intelligently search and reason across multiple documents — like a complex research task.
concepts.why_innovative: It is the first benchmark specifically designed to distinguish whether AI agents are genuinely planning their search or just randomly trying things, filling a critical gap that existing benchmarks missed.

concepts.label: accuracy-effort trade-off metric
concepts.description: A new measurement approach that tracks not just whether an AI gets the right answer, but how much work (number of search steps) it took to get there — rewarding efficient, targeted reasoning over brute-force trying.
concepts.why_innovative: This enables a fairer comparison between agents and humans by exposing that some AI systems waste enormous effort getting the same score as a human who searches much more efficiently.

concepts.label: agentic document collection vqa
concepts.description: A formal task definition where an AI must search across a collection of multi-page PDF documents, combining visual and text understanding, to answer questions that require visiting multiple documents and pages.
concepts.why_innovative: It formalizes a realistic enterprise workflow — researching across document archives — that prior AI tasks ignored, creating a standard foundation for measuring genuinely complex AI document reasoning.

concepts.label: classical test theory splits
concepts.description: A principled method borrowed from educational testing to select which questions go into the evaluation set, prioritizing questions that best separate strong AI systems from weak ones.
concepts.why_innovative: It ensures the benchmark stays useful as AI improves over time by reserving the hardest questions in a 'Sentinel Pool,' preventing top models from saturating the benchmark too quickly.

concepts.label: sentinel pool
concepts.description: A reserved subset of the hardest benchmark questions that no current AI model can answer, intentionally kept separate to guarantee the benchmark remains challenging as AI capabilities improve.
concepts.why_innovative: This design prevents AI leaderboards from becoming obsolete overnight — by baking in future headroom, it ensures the benchmark remains a meaningful challenge for next-generation models.

concepts.label: construct validity framework
concepts.description: A rigorous quality-checking process that verifies the benchmark actually tests what it claims to test — for example, confirming that questions genuinely require multi-step reasoning and not just keyword matching.
concepts.why_innovative: Most AI benchmarks skip this validation step, leading to inflated scores; applying it here ensures that high performance on MADQA truly reflects intelligent reasoning, not shortcuts.

concepts.label: multi-hop cross-document retrieval
concepts.description: Questions that can only be answered by combining information found in separate, unconnected pages or entirely different documents — like adding up figures that appear in two different annual reports.
concepts.why_innovative: This directly tests the hardest real-world research skill — synthesizing scattered evidence — exposing that current AI agents fail at this while humans handle it naturally.
